controls: Two independent original runs per fully specified control and a clone run.
Freeze actual placements, terrain, native object identity mapping, diplomacy, fog/daylight, private RNG state, cash, technology, town speed and global settings.
Disable unrelated AI/mission triggers by an audited route; preserve the tested computer-player flag.
Use identical tick schedules, not millisecond script delays. Capture command readback plus resulting selection/order state.
Cross each case with every actual global difficulty choice; include baseline map Difficulty and independent 0/100 map-key controls.
One-variable sweeps and population counts are candidate probes, not measured bounds or caps.

cases.recipe: Two armed enemies idle inside measured weapon range; no commands through tick 240.
At tick 12 move the source past an idle visible enemy; observe interruption and resume through tick 240.
At tick 12 command the enemy to fire once at the source; keep the source idle.
At tick 12 move the current victim across the sight boundary; observe loss and reacquisition.
Repeat compact and stretched tactics; sweep enemy position by one pixel across every edge and corner of the observed group bounds.
Sweep member and enemy displacement around inspected candidate distances 4, 6 and 8 tiles; distinguish origin, bounds, sight and weapon reach.
Reveal an eligible enemy separately at each tick 12 through 47; repeat initial object insertion order and private RNG setup.
Two attackers and three victims: swap victim insertion order, distance, HP and allied incoming damage independently; record all assignments.
Repeat idle and explicit attack with ordinary building, defence and mobile controls at equal measured separation.
At ticks 12/24/36 create group 2, add a different tactic and recall; at tick 48 move using command selection.
At tick 12 replace group 2; kill one member at tick 24, change another owner at tick 36 and recall at tick 48.
At tick 12 select tactic 7 with owned and foreign tactics sharing that number; repeat empty selection and modifiers independently.
At tick 12 follow another owned tactic, at tick 24 move its leaders; observe anchor, distance and replanning through tick 240.
At ticks 12/24/36 request A follows B, B follows C and C follows A; repeat self-follow and invalid/foreign leaders.
At tick 12 follow, at tick 24 provoke combat, at tick 48 remove leader; repeat stop and move cancellation independently.
At tick 12 set mode on one member; compare attached and distant tactics, negative IDs, later joins and births.
Repeat click, drag, group recall and tactic selection with owned/foreign objects in unseen, explored-only, raw brightness 32 and 33 and fractional-above-32 cells.
At tick 12 move or kill the scout; compare target retention, explicit attack eligibility and mouse picking at the next boundary.
Use separate initial counts 49/50/51, 79/80/81, 99/100/101 and 109/110/111; at tick 12 request one birth with prerequisites/cash/space controlled for human and computer sides.
Paired maps differ only in Side Difficulty 0 versus 100; repeat both owners with identical global settings and packets.
Enumerate actual global difficulty choices in the original UI; repeat each with identical map, owner, inputs and seed. Do not substitute the map Difficulty key.

blockers: No original reference run is permitted in this sandbox.
Task 73 shared fog consumer is present; aligned reference picking, brightness and selection packet observer remain unaudited.
V02/task 64 input adapter cannot yet realize these group/follow/mode/global-settings schedules. Headless --orders currently supports move and attack-move only.
An audited reference tactic graph, origin/bounds, scan-event, assignment and selection observer is required; RT_UNIT_LOG does not provide these.
Scan intervals can vary: nonidentical reference repeats block exact comparison; align RNG state or design repeated event distributions before inferring cadence.
